title: SLO-driven hybrid prefill and kernel handoff to reduce embedding p99
creator: Aisha Khan
description: Goal: Reduce embedding endpoint p99 latency for multi-tenant reranking workloads while preserving throughput and embedding quality. Background: We observe recurring p99 spikes during short bursts when small requests miss the KV prefill and then execute on a slow int8 kernel path. This ticket implements an SLO-driven hybrid prefill + hedged microbatch strategy and a fastpath kernel handoff mechanism to steer latency-sensitive requests to lower-latency execution paths without destabilizing overall throughput.
acceptance_criteria: p99 for 128B embedding requests <= 200ms on standard tenant profile for 24h of production traffic (compared to baseline ~420ms)
no degradation in mean embedding similarity quality (retrieval MRR) beyond 0.5% on reranking testset
end-to-end cost delta within +10% of baseline for typical traffic profiles
automated canary rollout + automatic rollback on 3% error-rate increase or 30% p99 regression
observability: dashboard showing request path split (prefill fastpath vs slowpath), per-kernel latency histograms, and hedging hit rate
tasks: Profile tail events and categorize root causes (prefill miss, kernel slowdown, queueing)
Implement SLO-driven prefill: maintain small per-tenant warm prefix cache with eviction policy tied to 95th latency SLO
Add hedged microbatching: launch a speculative fastpath attempt against a small fast-queue after X ms timeout
Introduce kernel handoff API: attach kernel hints to requests and allow runtime to migrate to fast int4/int8 kernels when input shape and quantization metadata permit
Add telemetry: new tracing tags for prefill/hedge/hand_off and dashboard panels
Run staged canary on dedicated infra and evaluate p50/p95/p99 and retrieval quality
Roll out to 10% of tenants, monitor for 72h, then gradual ramp with automatic rollback guardrails
comments: 2025-01-16 - AK: Initial profiling completed. 80% of p99 events correlate with prefill misses followed by slow kernel selection on quantized shards.

2025-01-22 - LM: Prototype hedged microbatch implemented; local load tests show p99 drop from 420ms -> 190ms for small single-request bursts but with 6% extra token compute cost in worst-case hedged hits.
2025-01-29 - DataSci (Maya Patel): Verified reranking MRR on internal testset unchanged within 0.3% across hedged and kernel-handoff flows.
2025-02-03 - Infra (J. Ortega): Kernel handoff API landed in runtime branch 'kernel-handoff/eng-987654' (PR #4521). Observability tags added to agent traces.
2025-02-05 - AK: Canary started at 5% of tenants. Early telemetry: hedged hit-rate 4.2%, prefill warm-hit increased to 68% from 44%. p99 median reduction ~210ms; continuing monitoring.
decision_log: 2025-01-20: Decided to prioritize latency SLO (p99) over micro-optimizations that only impact p50. Rationale: reranking customers are highly sensitive to p99 when using real-time inference.
2025-01-25: Chose hedged microbatch approach vs aggressive batching because batching increased p50 but hurt p99 for single-request bursts. Hedging yields lower p99 at bounded cost.
2025-02-01: Opted for conservative kernel handoff policy: require shape and quant metadata checks and a short stabilization window to avoid oscillation.
qa_plan: Synthetic replay of peak-day traffic (from 2025-01-10 incident) with labeled reranking testset
A/B quality evaluation comparing retrieval MRR and downstream click-simulated metric over 1M queries
Chaos test: simulate cold-cache eviction and network jitter to ensure rollback triggers function
notes: Risk: Hedging increases compute cost on hedged-hit paths. Mitigation: adaptive hedging throttle tied to tenant spend tier and observed benefit.

Implementation detail: kernel handoff will leverage existing kernel registry and add 'preferred_latency_budget_ms' hint; runtime will pre-select candidate kernels and attach handoff tokens to requests.
Follow-ups: consider tenant-level adaptive prefill size and ML-driven heatmap for prioritizing warm entries (separate ticket)
